newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. rate fears drag down Manila stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rate fears drag down Manila stocks at close.

text.p: Manila stocks ended lower on Tuesday on fears of a U.S. rate hike, brokers said.
"Bright prospects in the local economy remained intact. It's the prospects of a possible U.S. rate increase that is dragging down the local market," said Juanis Barredo at Citisecurities.
The main index dropped 41.50 points, or by 1.28 percent, to 3,207.89.
Manila brokers said they expected most foreign fund managers to trade sideways until they get clearer signals on where U.S. interest rates are heading in the next several days.
The U.S. market was closed on Monday for Labour Day.
Volume in Manila was moderate with some 1.3 billion pesos worth of shares changing hands.
Brokers said they see the market finding its support at the 3,100 barrier before it treks back upwards.
